quote.text: Every soul, the philosopher says, is involuntarily deprived of truth; consequently in the same way it is deprived of justice and temperance and benevolence and everything of the kind. It is most necessary to bear this constantly in mind, for thus thou wilt be more gentle towards all.
quote.author: Marcus Aurelius
quote.aiInsight:
• Parenthood
    • Recognize that just as every soul is imperfect, our children are learning and evolving, and thus we must lead with patience and gentle guidance.
    • Embrace the idea that imperfection fosters growth—by accepting our own limitations and those of our offspring, we nurture an environment rich in empathy and understanding.
  • Leadership
    • Understand that every individual, including those we lead, is inherently flawed; this awareness calls for a leadership style rooted in compassion rather than harsh judgment.
    • Accept that striving for absolute truth and perfection in others is futile—instead, cultivate a culture of continual learning, patience, and benevolent correction.
  • Product Management
    • As products and processes are born of human endeavor, acknowledge their imperfection from the start; this recognition encourages iterative improvements without undue blame.
    • Apply gentle persistence in development, balancing high standards with the understanding that every decision and outcome carries inherent limitations, much like the human soul in its quest for truth.
